sections.overview: The Rufous-fronted Laughingthrush is a critically endangered songbird endemic to Java, Indonesia.
sections.identification: Its grey plumage and conspicuous rufous forehead patch distinguish it from other laughingthrushes.
sections.habitat: It is associated with montane forest on Java; conservation records span highland sites in West Java and Mount Slamet.
sections.diet: Detailed wild diet data are scarce; captive guidelines describe a softbill diet with fruit, insects and other foods.
sections.behavior: The 2013 conservation note reports few reliable recent records and emphasizes the need for field surveys.
sections.reproduction: Breeding biology in the wild remains poorly known; EAZA guidelines document managed captive breeding and husbandry.
sections.ecology: Two named subspecies are recognized in conservation sources, including slametensis from Mount Slamet, not recorded in the wild since 1925.
sections.conservation: BirdLife assesses the species as Critically Endangered; trapping for the cage-bird trade is identified as a major pressure.
